title: Thai Yellow Coconut Curry with Prawns, Potatoes and Crispy Shallots
summary: Potatoes are parboiled, yellow curry paste is fried in thick coconut milk until the oil separates, then thinned coconut milk, palm sugar, fish sauce, potatoes, cherry tomatoes and prawns are simmered briefly and topped with crispy shallots.

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into 4 cm chunks
store-bought Thai yellow curry paste (check the label is halal)
palm sugar or light brown sugar
fish sauce (check the label is halal)
large raw prawns, peeled and deveined

steps.title: Fry the shallots
steps.text: Fry the shallots slowly in oil until golden, then drain to crisp.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Simmer the potatoes in unsalted water until just tender and drain.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Fry the paste in thick coconut milk added in stages until it darkens and the oil separates.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the sugar, fish sauce and thinned coconut milk, then the potatoes and tomatoes.

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Simmer the prawns until pink, opaque and 63 °C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with crispy shallots and serve with jasmine rice.

tips: Lift the shallots out when light gold; they darken off the heat.
Do not overcook the prawns or they turn tough.
Taste before adding more fish sauce; pastes vary.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and eat within 1 day, reheated gently until piping hot. Keep the shallots separate and airtight. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
